newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's interbank rate to rise - Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's interbank rate to rise - Salomon.

text.p: Salomon Brothers said on Wednesday Singapore's three-month interbank rate was likely to recover to 3.25 percent in six months.
"With economic growth showing clear signs of recovery, the authorities are likely to maintain their cautious stance on lending, particularly on mortgages," it said in a weekly research report.
Singapore's three-month interbank rate was expected to rebound to 3.25 percent from the current 2.8 percent, the report said.
It said forecasts for a 25-50 basis point increase in the U.S. Federal Funds rate by mid-year suggested Singapore's interbank rates would probably rise.
"Singapore's interest rates are likely to rise by the same magnitude in order to maintain the Singapore-US interest rate differential and hence, the exchange rate," it said.
The three-month interbank rate was kept in the range of 3.0 to 3.5 percent in the second half of last year.
But the rate experienced a sharp fall, reaching 2.5 percent in mid-February before rebounding to 2.8 percent, it said.
It added that a small rise in inflation, although relatively low at 2.0 percent year-to-year in January 1997, did not support a lower interest rate climate.
The report said the recent decline in Singapore's interbank rate was caused mainly by external factors and likely to be temporary.
Rates adjusted downwards on short-term capital inflows when there was an increase in risk premium to the Thai baht led by recent fears of devaluation, it said.
